narrativeProgression.description: The teacher begins by explaining the problem
He draws a pentagon on the blackboard to represent the problem
He labels the points of the pentagon with 'q' to represent the charges
He draws lines from the center of the pentagon to each point to show the forces acting on the center charge
He labels each angle of the pentagon with '72' to show the symmetry of the pentagon
He labels the top point of the pentagon with '[q]' to represent a hypothetical charge
He draws arrows to represent forces from each point of the pentagon, showing the direction of the forces
He circles the bottom left corner of the pentagon and labels it '+q' to represent a test charge at the center of the pentagon
He labels each side of the pentagon 'a' to represent the distance between the charges
He writes an equation on the blackboard to calculate the magnitude of the force exerted by each charge
He draws lines to represent forces coming from the pentagon on the right side of the blackboard, representing the forces in a different way
He draws a closed shape with arrows, showing that the forces cancel each other out
He explains that the force due to all five charges is zero
He explains that if you remove the fifth charge, the force will not be zero
He explains that if you place the fifth charge back, the force will be zero again
He writes an equation on the blackboard to show that the magnitude of the force exerted by one charge is equal to the magnitude of the force exerted by the four charges combined
